tasks.short: Complete the reports and forms that finalize a case.

steps.what: Gather notes needed to finalize cases.
Decide the forms required to finalize cases.
Complete the accepted reports and forms.

tasks.design: The coroner gathers the notes, decides which reports and forms the case requires, and accepts them. The file then completes those forms from the notes they already wrote. It does not decide that the case is ready, and it does not invent a sentence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Which form a case needs depends on the manner of death and on the local register, which a fixed pack gets wrong.
tasks.enabler_now: Fields that are already in the coroner's notes can be placed on the form they have accepted.
tasks.still_hard: A form filed early, or with a sentence the coroner did not write, becomes part of the record.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner decides the forms and accepts the text. The file only places accepted fields.
tasks.altitude: Choosing and accepting the reports stays with the coroner. Completing a form means copying fields they have already accepted.

reach.task: Send a form the coroner has accepted
reach.learn: The coroner decided which forms the case required

evidence.claim: Form fields can be copied from notes the coroner already wrote, after they have accepted which forms the case needs.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the case notes exist and ends when the accepted forms are on the file. Signing a certificate, where the register requires it, stays outside it.
The fields are case id, the form name the coroner chose, and the values taken from their notes. The coroner produces the choice and the values. A value that is not in the notes is left blank.
The prior treats the task as automate. The steps disagree in part: deciding which forms are required, and accepting them, stay with the coroner. Only the placement of accepted fields is machine.
Upkeep is keeping the form names aligned with what the register currently asks for.
unknowns: Which forms this register requires for each manner of death.
Whether some forms must still be signed on paper.
research_questions: Which forms does the register require for each manner of death?
Which forms must still be signed on paper?

already_counted.description: Deciding the required forms stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the form names aligned with the register

approvals.approved_version: reports and forms the coroner accepted after deciding they were required

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the notes are thin and most of the form is still written by hand, the low end is that writing plus the decision of which forms are required, which stays. A sentence is never added. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange for the next of kin to be notified.

steps.what: Find who must be notified of the deaths.
Arrange for the next of kin to be notified.
Confirm a person will see that kin are notified.
Note the plan to arrange notification of deaths.

tasks.design: The coroner finds who must be told and arranges for a person to notify them. The note records that arrangement. No message goes out by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right person is not always the first name on a form, and some deaths must be told in a particular way.
tasks.enabler_now: The name of the person who will do the telling can be written once.
tasks.still_hard: Telling the wrong person, or telling them by a message, can be cruel and can harm the investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner arranges the notification. A contact list does not send it.
tasks.altitude: Arranging the notification stays with the coroner. The note only records the arrangement they made.

reach.task: Tell the next of kin the coroner named
reach.learn: The coroner arranged who would speak

evidence.claim: A note can name the person the coroner asked to notify the next of kin. It does not notify them.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a death must be notified and ends when the arrangement is noted. The conversation with the relative is a separate task, unless the coroner does that telling themselves.
The fields are case id and the name of the person who will notify. The coroner produces the name by finding them. No message text is generated.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. The note is a small remainder of an arrangement already made.
Upkeep is keeping the roles that are allowed to notify a relative.
unknowns: Which roles are allowed to notify a next of kin.
Which deaths the coroner must notify in person.
research_questions: Which roles may notify a next of kin?
Which deaths must the coroner notify in person?

already_counted.description: Arranging the notification stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the roles that are allowed to notify a relative

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the coroner almost always makes the call themselves, the note shrinks and the low end is finding the person and arranging the call, which stay. No message is sent by a tool. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Locate next of kin and document the attempts.

steps.what: Record their relationship to the deceased.
Record the status of notification attempts.
Review that information before it is filed.

tasks.design: The coroner locates the next of kin, records the relationship and the status of each attempt, and reviews that information. The file then stores it. It does not search for relatives and it does not mark an attempt the coroner did not make.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating a person is a search across incomplete records, and a similar name is a common error.
tasks.enabler_now: Relationship and attempt status, once the coroner has written them, need not be copied by hand a second time.
tasks.still_hard: The wrong relative, or a false 'notified', changes who is told and what the file claims.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner locates the person and records what was tried. The file stores that.
tasks.altitude: Locating kin and recording each attempt stay with the coroner. The file documents the information they reviewed.

reach.task: Use a kin record the coroner reviewed
reach.learn: The coroner located the person and logged each attempt

evidence.claim: Relationship and attempt status can be stored after the coroner has located the person and written them down.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when kin must be found and ends when the reviewed information is on the file. Speaking to the relative is a separate task.
The fields are case id, name, relationship, and the status of each attempt. The coroner produces them. An attempt they did not make is not added.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on locating and on writing the attempts. Only the copy of reviewed information is shorter.
Upkeep is keeping the attempt-status labels the office uses.
unknowns: Which registers the coroner may search when locating kin.
How many attempts are made before the office stops.
research_questions: Which registers may the coroner search to locate kin?
How many attempts are made before the office stops?

already_counted.description: Locating the next of kin stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the attempt-status labels the office uses

approvals.approved_version: kin information the coroner reviewed after locating them and recording each attempt

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If locating someone rarely produces a clean name, the low end is the search and the writing, which stay, and the file copy is rare. No search runs itself. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect and document the medical history.
tasks.design: The coroner collects the medical history from records and from clinicians, reviews what is pertinent, and the file documents that accepted history. It does not request records and it does not add a diagnosis.
tasks.previous_blocker: What is pertinent depends on the death, and a record from a clinic is not always the history that matters.
tasks.enabler_now: History the coroner has collected and marked as pertinent can be placed on the file once.
tasks.still_hard: A diagnosis the coroner did not collect would sit in the file as if it were fact.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner collects the history and decides what is pertinent. The file does not.
tasks.altitude: Collecting the history stays with the coroner. The file documents only the history they reviewed as pertinent.

reach.task: Answer a history request the coroner made
reach.learn: The coroner decided what was pertinent

evidence.claim: Medical history the coroner has collected can be stored after they have reviewed what is pertinent. A diagnosis is not added.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when history is needed and ends when the reviewed history is on the file. The examination is a separate task.
The fields are case id, source, and the history lines the coroner marked. The coroner produces the lines by collecting them. A line that was not in the source is not written.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on collecting and reviewing. Only the copy of the reviewed history is shorter.
Upkeep is keeping the list of clinics that release records to this office.
unknowns: Which clinics release records to this office, and on what request.
Whether the coroner or a clinician marks a line as pertinent.
research_questions: Which clinics release records to this office?
Who marks a line as pertinent, the coroner or a clinician?

already_counted.description: Collecting the medical history stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the list of clinics that release records

approvals.approved_version: medical history the coroner reviewed after collecting it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the history arrives as paper and must be read line by line, the low end is that reading and the collection, which stay. Nothing is added that the coroner did not collect. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The coroner decides which forms a case needs, who must be notified, and which history is pertinent. Forms and history are copied only from what they collected and accepted. Notification is arranged by them, not sent for them.
reach: A records clerk sends a form the coroner accepted
A clinician answers a history request the coroner made
skills_to_grow: Deciding the required forms before they are completed
Locating kin without a search that picks the person
Marking history as pertinent before it is documented
role.ambitious_version: Every form on a finalized case is one the coroner decided was required, and every notification was arranged by a person.
